image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Curved section of elevated expressway deck bending clearly to one side in plan like one eighth of a ring, a deep trapezoidal concrete box girder sweeping through the arc under a wide road slab whose solid parapets on both edges follow the curve, flat soffit, drain pipe along the outer edge, three curving asphalt lanes on top Materials: Pale grey precast concrete with segment joint lines, soot and rust drip streaks on the soffit, grey asphalt with curved white dashed lines and a yellow edge line, grimy parapet.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless pure WHITE studio matte (#ffffff), so that the grey concrete stands out clearly against it. The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91. 1,204/32,000 triangles, 4/24 draw calls, 4/16 materials, 4/32 unique geometries, three canvases.

featureReviews.evidence: Bounds x -6.25..8.82, y 0..3.5, z -8.09..9.71 off the built module (the pipe's entry ring adds 0.09): a 40 m radius through 22.5 degrees with the entry face a straight module's and the exit at (3.045, 0, 7.307) yawed 22.5.
Lane lines follow the arc (v fixed on an arc-length u); joints every 2.67 m of arc; both parapets curve with the section exact at all 12 stations.
Probed on beauty-hero: road 144 (plate 140), parapet 136 (136), web 168 (plate 200 sunlit). Soot bands, the pipe tube along the outer arc with three brackets.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's web at 200 is a white-backed sunlit reading; the render holds 168 so it does not blow out.

name: Expressway Deck Curve Segment
nameTh: พื้นสะพานทางด่วนโค้ง
notes: A 22.5 degree turn so four make a right angle. MODULAR CONTRACT for the highway set: the deck's centreline is an arc of radius 40 m turning 22.5 degrees (arc length 15.7 m), entering along -Z at the pivot end and leaving rotated 22.5 degrees about Y; the ENTRY face is at z=-8-equivalent, i.e. the module is positioned like a straight module with its pivot at the SOFFIT centre of the entry-end chord so it butts a straight module placed at the same y=12; road surface at pivot+2.40, parapet top at pivot+3.50; slab 12.5 m wide, box girder 7 m wide. The exit end's position and yaw must be written into notes after the build so the level editor user can chain the next piece. Bbox 17 x 15.5 is the arc's extent, not a straight width.
